## Restored class definitions

Added in candidate: verbatim restoration of `docs/architect/host-invocation-routing/external-provider-protocol.md` at `83d757f4d693ae13d3fd50e0a454fb95c78f1ff4`; preservation is not a fresh implementation claim.

**Checked status:** The class/mechanism axes are preserved as design policy. ProviderDescriptor stores open string metadata; this citation does not prove every release/authority policy or example pack is enforced or shipped.

**Code evidence:** `packages/host-runtime/rust/src/contracts.rs:377-393`.

````md
**Core component** — required for a useful fgOS release; owned by fgOS, released atomically with the host, normally statically linked once migrated. Not optional and not replaceable by default; may expose extension points, but a plugin implementing one does not become the authority owner of the core component. Examples: Work Lifecycle, Host Invocation, authority gating, provider routing, DispatchPlan selection, Assignment/Run/RunResult contracts, init/doctor health.
````

````md
**Packaged extension** — owned and shipped by fgOS but not required for a minimum useful release; may be enabled/disabled/omitted by configuration, edition, or environment. Follows fgOS release discipline, compatibility policy, init/doctor registration, docs, tests. More trustworthy than a user plugin because fgOS ships it, but disabling it must not corrupt core state or block boot. Examples: optional domain packages, optional coordination protocol packs, optional Herdr/dashboard surfaces.
````

````md
| Component class | Common invocation mechanism | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Core component | Built-in after migration; LegacyNode during transition | Required, fgOS-owned, atomically released. |
| Packaged extension | Built-in, ExternalProcess, or ExternalWasm | fgOS-owned but optional; install/init/doctor aware. |
| User plugin | ExternalProcess or ExternalWasm | User-owned, independently installed; manifest-linked and capability-gated. |
````

````md
This classification blocks two mistakes: treating every statically linked implementation as architecturally core, and treating every out-of-process implementation as a user plugin. Packaging and authority follow component class; runtime calling details follow invocation mechanism.
````

````md
```rust
enum Provider {
    BuiltIn(Arc<dyn OperationProvider>),
    ExternalProcess(ProcessRpcClient),
    ExternalWasm(WasmComponent),
}
```
````

````md
**Built-In** — a trusted Rust crate statically linked into the host binary, called through the `OperationProvider` trait. No serialization or cross-process cost; still obeys the owning port and authority boundary. Normal mechanism for core components, and may serve packaged extensions fgOS chooses to compile in.
````

````md
**External Process** — an independently installed, language-neutral plugin reached through persistent framed RPC (§3). Fits extensions needing filesystem, Git, network, subprocess, or other OS capabilities. Crash/restart and resource isolation are part of the adapter contract.
````

````md
**External WebAssembly** — a sandboxed plugin reached through a typed component interface such as WIT. Fits pure or tightly capability-scoped extensions. Required host functions are explicit capabilities, not ambient access.
````

````md
Native Rust dynamic libraries are not the default external mechanism: Rust has no stable ABI, and in-process third-party native code loses the crash/memory isolation process or WASM boundaries give.
````


| Release tree manifest uses normalized logical paths and refuses symlinks/case collisions in V1. | Settled for V1. |
| Project commands enter through stable local shims under workspace `.fgos/installation/bin/`. | Settled for V1. |
| Immutable release payloads live under a shared content-addressed machine/trust-domain release store, not under each worktree. | Settled for V1. |
| Activation is per workspace via `.fgos/installation/activation.json`; there is no single repository-wide active runtime pointer in V1. | Settled for V1. |

| Mutating invocations create lease files; `fgctl` may stage/verify during leases but refuses activation while a non-stale mutating lease exists. | Settled for V1. |

rows.verbatimPayload:
- **RUL77 (posture belongs to the capability, an agent executor declares no `for`, and each door carries one posture lane; supersedes RUL76 (`execute --for ` with a "must declare" gate), 2026-10-13).** An agent executor can do any kind of work, so no `for` list describes it, and a list on one was read as the posture of every dispatch to it (`docs/specs/confinement-authority.md` already said a direct executor call must carry a capability anchor and never infer the minimum from `executor.for`). `resolveCapabilityDetailsFromHints` reads `for` from tool executors only; on an agent executor it is inert (config still loads, so projects and worktrees that carry one keep dispatching) and `fgos doctor` names it under `executor-profile-warnings` (`executor..agent-for-inert`); the agent executors' `for` lists are gone from this repo's `.fgos/config.json` (`decide --for` routing unchanged: it reads `capabilities..prefer`). The CLI door `execute ` refuses before spawning when no `--for` is given (`capability-required`, listing the writing capabilities and the read-only door); programmatic callers (Assignment, Work) pass their own capability hints and are unchanged. `execute --for ` runs the invocation that capability `prefer`s for that executor, else the first plain cli invocation with no sandbox backend, instead of always the first cli invocation. That door leases no provider account, so it carries writing work only: a capability with required confinement is refused (`posture-needs-assignment`). Read-only work runs sandboxed as a Workflow unit with `writes: []` (`fgos workflow start --units`), which binds the read-only posture and leases the account (the architecture-advisory seats ran that way: `confined-bwrap`, login provisioned); `execute --contract --executor ` keeps a named provider and leases its account but runs unconfined, read-only by instruction only (measured: `execute openai --for code:review` on the bare door ran `codex-cli-bwrap` confined and got 401 with no login; the same read through `--contract --executor openai` answered, on `cli-spawn` with `confinement: null`). A sandboxed read-only door that also keeps a named provider does not exist yet. The calling agent answers Q1 (does it write? does a provider matter?) from prose doctrine in `core/skills/_shared/capability-matching.md`, with no classifier or workflow generator. Decided after an `architecture-advisory` run (`wf-run-1791875339761-10315b91`: framing and shaping with three blind seats and a synthesizer completed; critique was blocked by a Codex trust prompt, so no reviewed synthesis exists). Not built: a soft provider hint on `decide` (`--prefer`, the synthesizer's recommendation) — naming the executor on `execute` already lets a caller pick a provider, and the hint would change `bind()`, shared with Workflow binding; revisit when a caller needs "this provider if it can, else any". 4. **Write-back at removal.** When a dispatch opted in, the private home's ownership marker records `credentialWriteBack` (provider, account, source home, layout, runtime dir; names and paths only). One removal function serves the driver cleanup, the finalizer of a settled dispatch and the orphan reaper: before deleting a home whose marker asks for it, a login in the home that is newer than the source's is staged under `pending/` (atomic rename) and applied under the account lock, tried once without waiting; when the lock is busy, or nothing proves the copy is not newer (the source is unreadable, its entry cannot be identified, or the copy cannot be read for a reason that may pass, such as `node:sqlite` being unavailable: an omp store is then staged as plain files, write-ahead log included), it stays pending and the next refresh-ahead (or removal) applies it once it can be identified, even if the source still looks fresh, because the source's own refresh token may already be spent; a refresh-ahead that skips because the entry is unidentified applies the pending copies too, so the ones that have become identifiable clear. Pending copies are capped at five per account, the newest by staging time; a drop writes one stderr line `credential-pending-dropped` with a count only. If staging itself fails, the private home and its marker are kept (the removal reports failure, one stderr line with a fixed code and no path or value) so a later removal, the reaper's included, retries; only a copy proven malformed, or one the source was read to prove not newer, lets the home go. Each failed attempt is counted in the marker (`credentialKept`: attempts, first time, time of the last counted attempt; failures less than 15 minutes after the last counted one are not counted again, so a transient fault does not use the budget up); the marker is rewritten through a temp file and a rename, and a marker that is present but unreadable stops the removal. After five attempts the home is held: no further removal attempt and no deletion by age, however old. A held home is re-checked, under the account lock, when that account is next renewed (the temp roots searched are the same as doctor's: the default one plus each registered backend's own `tempRoot`; a home under a backend's separate `privateHomeRoot` is in none of them, so no check, repair, reaper or renewal sees it, and it is never deleted either) and by `fgos doctor --fix`, and only a home of the lock's own runtime directory: it is removed only when the source is readable and proves its login is not newer, or when that login can now be staged beside the source (and is applied); otherwise it stays held. It also stays held when the pending copies are already full and its login would only be staged, so the cap never pushes out an older copy; a staged copy and the pending directory are synced to disk before the home goes. A marker file that is no recognisable marker at all (not JSON, not an object, no contract name) stops any removal of its home. The finalizer compares the ownership marker's digest without `credentialKept` (a failed driver cleanup adds it after the digest was taken) and carries on with the dispatch's other resources past a home that cannot go (the dispatch is recorded as retained, with the home's reason). The doctor check `credential-copies-retained` reports, by provider and account, held homes (a failure, naming the home directory), homes still being retried and pending or scratch copies older than a day (warnings), with counts, ages and never a value; the check deletes nothing. Any other write-back problem is reported on stderr by a fixed code and never stops the removal. - **RUL79 (`fgos dispatch probe-account`: one account, every CLI, at the same moment, diagnostic only, 2026-10-13).** A dispatch failure on one CLI does not say whether the account (dead login, quota) or the CLI (trust prompt, sandbox, version bug) is at fault. `fgos dispatch probe-account --provider

--account [--executor ] [--invocation ] [--timeout-ms ]` (`src/runner/dispatch/provider-account-probe.mjs`) starts every invocation that runs as the account at once through the Assignment door a Workflow unit uses (read-only posture binding, invocation pinned by `cliOverride`, inventory narrowed to the one account so the lease cannot pick another and a quarantine still refuses, RUL75 (a rotating login is renewed once at the source and written back from a private home) renewal opt-in), with a trivial prompt, and reports per CLI an outcome class (`ok`, `blocked-trust-prompt`, `auth`, `quota`, `sandbox`, `timeout`, `other`), the evidence line, the assignment, run directory and pane, plus a verdict (`healthy`; `account-fault` when every CLI failed with `auth`/`quota`; `cli-fault` when one answered; `mixed`). An invocation runs as the account when it is confined with a private home whose CLI the account's credential layout logs in (`lease`), when its credential env names the account home (`env`), or when its id ends with `-` (`name`, the config's `--` convention). It closes the panes the rounds left open and removes the private homes kept for them; it picks and schedules nothing. First real run (openai/tetcu72): both Codex invocations `ok` (cli-spawn under bwrap and the herdr pane), both pi invocations `sandbox` (`EROFS` on `~/.pi/accounts/openai-tetcu72/settings.json.lock`: under the read-only posture pi cannot write its own account directory, which it does before answering; outside confinement the same pi account answered), verdict `cli-fault`.

Binding/posture resolution is policy/provenance evidence, not live confinement proof. Retained cognitive doctrine is not a claim of end-to-end specialist, dialogue, distinct per-seat tasks, final-packet review or interrupted-Unit continuity; those gaps belong to the separate [advisory completion plan](../../plans/261006-1408-advisory-capability-completion/plan.md), not this single-door hygiene cleanup.

rows.verbatimPayload: **Vai mù thật sự (`blind`) — chặn đọc run state của peer.** Mặc định tắt (không đổi hành vi). Một cờ ở Unit (và ở `template` của Workflow): `blind: true` làm *mọi vai* của Unit chạy với `hostRead: blind` (`docs/specs/confinement-authority.md` §9.2): worker không đọc được `.fgos/assignments`, `.fgos/workflow-runs`, `.fgos/dispatch-runs` của project, thư mục socket herdr, private home của dispatch khác, hay `/proc/<pid>` của tiến trình anh em; chỉ đọc được thư mục của chính nó (brief, ref đã được trao — chỉ-đọc) và ghi outbox. Phần còn lại của host (repo, `node`, DNS) và file tracked trong `.fgos` không đổi. Unit `blind` không bao giờ chạy không-blind: nếu không thực thi được — `bind()` không chọn in-process/inline, không có bwrap, mode không `required`, probe hỏng/chưa tươi, `cwd` hay ref nằm trong vùng bị che — dispatch bị từ chối trước khi spawn với lý do có tên (`blind-in-process`, `blind-requires-confinement`, `blind-hides-workspace`, `blind-ref-hidden`, `confinement-probe-failed`, ...). Với Unit `blind`, input `unit-run:`/`gate-answer:` (và ref bất kỳ nằm trong vùng bị che) không được giao bằng đường dẫn gốc: lúc dispatch, `resolveUnitInputs` + `copyHandoffsInto` chép nguyên byte (kiểm sha256) vào `inputs/` của round dir của chính vai đó, mỗi vai một bản, tên trung tính khi có `anonymizeInputs`; `unit.json` giữ `inputMap`, resume dùng lại bản chép. `blind-ref-hidden` chỉ còn cho ref không chép được. Workflow bật `blind`: hai bước panel của `delphi` (`propose-round-1`, `propose-round-2`), `generate-ideas` của `nominal-group`, `sense-making-panel` của `group-cognition`; `architecture-advisory` và `business-discussion` chưa bật vì pool của chúng gồm agy, họ chưa qua canary blind.

rows.verbatimPayload: - **RUL90 (the raw dispatch doors are removed; dispatch is the lower layer and fanout belongs to the Work layer, 2026-10-14; decision 0062, replaces the purpose-door part of RUL68 (2 tầng dispatch) and the one-posture-lane-per-door part of RUL77 (posture belongs to the capability)).** Work is executed through two doors only, `fgos run` (`"<prompt>"`, `--unit`, `--resume`) and `fgos workflow start`, both on `runUnit`. `dispatch execute` (executor id, `--contract`, `--assignment`), `dispatch log` and `dispatch fanout-batch` are gone, with `src/runner/dispatch-log.mjs`; calling `dispatch execute` (any form) or `dispatch log` returns a `validation` error with one sentence naming the replacement (`fgos run "<prompt>" [--provider <executor>] [--capability <c>] [--writes …]` or `fgos run --unit`, where `--provider` is named only for an agent executor — `fgos run` refuses any other kind — the `--for` capability is kept when it is registered, and a tool executor's caller is told to call that tool directly; the dispatch-decide hook's BLOCKED message is built the same way, by `runDoorHint`; `fgos run --unit` or a Workflow for `--assignment`; provenance under `.fgos/assignments/<unitRunId>/` for `dispatch log`), from one place in `bin`, also for `returnResult` callers. `executeExecutorCli` has no CLI door left: it is the transport step of an Assignment (`assignment-runner.mjs`), and its one other caller, `fanout-batch.mjs`, is listed in `R3_PENDING_WORK_CALLERS` until fanout runs on `runUnit`; `fgos dispatch` keeps `decide`, `inspect`, `reconcile` and `probe-account`. `src/runner/dispatch.mjs` imports nothing from the Work layer: `decide --work` gets its Work resolver injected from `bin`, so it runs only as `fgos dispatch decide --work`. A Unit's posture comes from its `writes` (none: read-only, sandboxed; some: mutating, in a linked worktree) plus the capability's required confinement, never from which door was used. Fanout adds no verb: `node src/runner/fanout-batch.mjs "<ids>" [--has-live-task-access]` prints `fired`, `mechanismChanged`, `unavailable`, `deferred` (plus `slotsFull: true` when no slot was free); its body moves onto `runUnit` with the Work-layer cut. An import guard (`test/architecture.test.mjs`) keeps `dispatch.mjs` and `src/workflow/**` free of Work imports, following relative imports transitively (a re-export one or more hops away counts) and reading `require()` and literal `import()`; a call-site guard over `src`, `bin`, `scripts`, `domains` and `core` names the files allowed to call `executeAssignment`, `executeExecutorCli`, `commitUnitWork` and `executeThroughConfinement` (an aliased, destructured or namespace use counts as a call; `export *` from their home modules is refused), with Work-layer callers not yet on `runUnit` listed in `R3_PENDING_WORK_CALLERS`, compared by equality so the list can only shrink. An `import()` with a non-literal specifier is not yet seen by the import guard (left to the dispatch-generic-inputs phase). - `src/runner/main-checkout-lock.mjs` (STR65) — `acquireMainCheckoutLock(dir, {identity, ttlMs, now})`/`releaseMainCheckoutLock(dir)`: khóa tạo-nguyên-tử `wx` + đòi-lại-pid-chết, độc lập với ba khóa anh em (`runner.lock`/`sessions.lock`/`events.lock`, không import chung, xem lineage note ở `src/state/events.mjs`); `identity` nhận số nguyên (pid thật, kiểm sống qua tín hiệu 0) HOẶC chuỗi (danh tính phiên, không kiểm sống được); TỰ-NHẬN-DIỆN: danh tính khóa hiện có trùng đúng danh tính người gọi → luôn ACQUIRED (refresh), bất kể ttlMs/sống-chết — đây là "chính phiên này tiếp tục", không phải một chủ cạnh tranh; danh tính KHÁC: số nguyên giữ nguyên phép thử sống+ttl có sẵn, chuỗi chỉ xét độ mới theo `ttlMs` (không có gì để kiểm sống); nội dung khóa hỏng/không phân tích được → AMBIGUOUS (không bao giờ coi là rảnh hay đang giữ). Manifest layer: infra.
- `.githooks/pre-commit` (STR65) — hook git-native (không phải verb fgOS, không phải cấu hình riêng công cụ trợ lý nào — xem "Khóa hoạt động cây chính" trên cho hợp đồng đầy đủ): giải thư mục gốc worktree bằng `path.resolve(__dirname, '..')` (KHÔNG gọi `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` — biến môi trường `GIT_DIR` mà git tự đặt khi hook chạy TRONG một git worktree làm lời gọi đó trả sai thư mục gốc, xác nhận thật bằng tái tạo có chủ đích trước khi vá); gọi `resolveWriterIdentity()` rồi `acquireMainCheckoutLock` với `ttlMs` mặc định 300000 (5 phút, đọc đè được qua biến môi trường `FGOS_MAIN_CHECKOUT_LOCK_TTL_MS`) — số này chọn từ bằng chứng thật (khoảng cách giữa các commit thật của 3 sự cố STR65 có SHA, ~2-3.5 phút), giảm từ mức mặc định 15 phút ban đầu qua 10 phút xuống 5 phút; HELD/AMBIGUOUS → in thông điệp bằng thời gian + trỏ `docs/how-to-parallel-lanes.md`, thoát khác 0; ACQUIRED → thoát 0 im lặng.
